schema_documentation:
3 top-level keys, all 100% present, single schema across all 2,883 sampled records.

| key | type | presence | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | str | 100% | document chunk — THE training field |
| `id` | str | 100% | byte-identical to `metadata.url` (verified 667/667 records across all three folders) — a Wikipedia URL, an Eurlex CELEX path, or `<book_id>_<chunk_n>` |
| `metadata` | dict | 100% | 18 sub-keys |

**metadata sub-keys** (all 100% present): `name` = `common_corpus` (constant); `collection` str enum of 19 — measured over 4,800 records: Eurlex 46.5%, Wikipedia 33.6%, Greek-PD 10.0%, Eurovoc 7.6%, Marianne-Europe 0.7%, Europeana 0.4%, then Multilingual-PD / German-PD / US-PD-Books / TEDEUTenders / French-PD-diverse / LoC-PD-Books / French-Science-Pile / Youtube-Commons / German-Science-Pile / Italian-PD / French Open Data / English-PD / Open-Science-Pile each ≤0.2%; `open_type` enum {Open Government 54.9%, Open Web 33.7%, Open Culture 11.2%, Open Science 0.1%}; `license` enum {CC-By 54.1%, CC-By-SA 33.6%, Public Domain 11.2%, Various open data 0.9%, Various open science 0.1%}; `date` float ~97.8% / null ~2.2% (range 1509–2023); `title` str 100% but the LITERAL STRING `"None"` for Eurlex; `creator` str 100%, also literal `"None"` for Eurlex, and a Wikipedia history URL for Wikipedia; `language` = `ell` (constant); `language_type` = `Spoken` (constant); `language_score` float; `language_script` = `Grek` (constant); `word_count` int; `token_count` int; `url` str (= `id`); `dataset` = `PleIAs/common_corpus` (constant); `file_path` str (upstream .jsonl.gz path, 21 distinct values); `shard_id` str (14 distinct); `__index_level_0__` int (pandas index residue).
semantic_meaning: Modern-Greek slice of PleIAs common_corpus: EU legislation (Eurlex/Eurovoc), Greek Wikipedia, and scanned public-domain books, chunked to ~40–50K chars.
